{SHl}.found: rnams ooo ka re lhan du gsungs
{SHl}.expected: rnams shlooo ka re lhan du gsungs
{SHl}.evidence: The wylie conversion drops the ACIP Sanskrit brace code {SHl} (sh with subjoined la), leaving the orphan `ooo ka`, which cannot be a Tibetan syllable sequence - no consonant, and a tripled vowel letter. The acip field of this same row preserves the source: "SKYE BA KUN TU RNAMS {SHl}OOO KA RE LHAN DU GSUNGS,". Measured over the whole spine: 23 rows carry a {SHl} brace code and all 23 lose the `shl` in their wylie (count of rows where acip matches '%{SHl}OO%' and wylie matches '%oo ka%' but not '%shl%' = 23 of 23); by contrast 9 rows spell the word without the brace code as SHLOO KA and all 9 keep it, wylie `shloo ka` (e.g. TITLS:1252 acip "...POD SO SOR SHLOO KA RE" -> wylie "...pod so sor shloo ka re"; also C03:349 and C07:80). Two of the damaged rows are in this same document: C03:302 acip "LHA YI SKAD DANG SOGS {SHl}OO KA RE RE" -> wylie "lha yi skad dang sogs oo ka re re"; C03:378 acip "ZHES PA'I {SHl}OO KA GCIG STE" -> wylie "zhes pa'i oo ka gcig ste". The word is Sanskrit shloka, "verse", which is what the English of this segment renders ("the various verses"). `expected` above is the converter-faithful output for this row's source as keyed; the residual tripled vowel is a separate source defect, filed below, after which the reading is `shloo ka`. Effect: the word is unsearchable and unreadable in the wylie layer in all 23 rows.

{SHl}.evidence: Confirmed from this segment's own text. ACIP (source of record) reads GO 'PANG; the wylie field carries the same reading, go 'pang, so this is in the source, not the converter. The word is go 'phang (rank, station, state), which is what GMR translates: 'the state of All-Knowing'. Re-derived corpus counts: acip LIKE '%GO ''PANG%' returns exactly one row, C03:445; acip LIKE '%GO ''PHANG%' returns 219; the wylie field splits identically, 1 vs 219. Stronger still, the syllable 'pang occurs NOWHERE else in the corpus wylie: a-chung ('a) prefixes only voiced or aspirated radicals in Tibetan orthography ('g 'j 'd 'b 'dz 'kh 'ch 'th 'ph 'tsh), so 'p- is not a spellable syllable onset and 'pang cannot be a variant. Parallel-witness check: no other segment carries this passage (english LIKE '%habit of hoping for the%', english LIKE '%up to the final end%', wylie LIKE '%tshe ''di snang gi zhen pa%', wylie LIKE '%rang res ngan ''gro%' each return C03:445 alone). The nearest relative for the surrounding idiom, ILL:126 (thog mtha' bar gsum du gal che), shares only that closing idiom and says nothing about go 'phang. Registered classes checked and not applicable: no {SHl} drop, no fused footnote number, no folio marker, no glued heading; the ACIP trailing shad ',' absent from the wylie is the normal strip, and ACIP TSE for wylie tshe is the ACIP convention (TS = tsh), not an error.
